title: Arts participation remains broad but physical engagement fell, digital substitution stalled, and deprivation and place shape access
source_unit: UK Department for Culture, Media and Sport, Community and Engagement Survey 2025/26: arts report
geography: England; representative survey of people aged 16 and over, with regional, local-authority and demographic breakdowns

observations.period: 2025/26; annual arts engagement and time series

denominator.unit: over 175,000 Community and Engagement Survey responses; headline estimates combine April 2025–March 2026 data from the Participation Survey and CES

overall_engagement.unit: percent of people aged 16+ engaging with the arts at least once in the prior 12 months

prior_year.unit: percent engaging with the arts in 2024/25

long_run_peak.unit: percent engaging with the arts in 2023/24

measurement_boundary.value: the report says it is unclear whether the decline is real or partly due to methodological differences between CES and the Participation Survey

observations.method: Continuous push-to-web Community and Engagement Survey combined with Participation Survey data for April 2025–March 2026; representative of people aged 16+ in England, with revised commentary updated September 16, 2026.
observations.uncertainty: Headline estimates combine survey instruments with different collection periods and question placement; the report explicitly says the apparent decline is under investigation.
observations.subgroup: People aged 16 and over in England, with demographic, regional and local-authority breakdowns.
observations.counterinterpretation: The 84% estimate may represent measurement discontinuity, changed question context, or sampling composition rather than a comparable collapse in arts participation.

denominator.unit: over 175,000 CES responses; people aged 16+ in England

physical_engagement.unit: percent engaging physically with the arts at least once in the prior 12 months, down from 90% in 2024/25

digital_engagement.unit: percent engaging digitally with the arts, broadly stable from 35% in 2024/25

both_modes.unit: percent of arts-engaged people engaging both physically and digitally

physical_only.unit: percent of arts-engaged people engaging exclusively physically

substitution_route.value: digital engagement has not expanded enough to compensate for the apparent physical-engagement decline

observations.method: Survey estimates for physical and digital arts participation using the report's combined 2025/26 data frame.
observations.uncertainty: Digital and physical categories are broad and may include different intensities; the combined survey design and question placement limit direct year-over-year interpretation.
observations.subgroup: People aged 16+ engaging with arts activities or events physically, digitally, or in both modes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Physical and digital engagement may be complementary rather than substitutable; stable digital participation does not show whether content, spending, attention or social connection remained stable.

denominator.unit: over 175,000 CES responses; subgroup estimates among non-engagers and people aged 16+

physical_cost_barrier.unit: percent of people not physically engaging who report they cannot afford it

digital_cost_barrier.unit: percent of people not digitally engaging who report they cannot afford it

local_authority_range.value: physical engagement ranged from 94% in Horsham to 69% in Barking and Dagenham

deprivation_gap.value: physical engagement was 70% in the most deprived decile versus 91% in the least deprived; digital engagement was 27% versus 41%

access_route.value: cultural participation is shaped by household room and place-based access, not only interest or cultural identity

observations.method: Published subgroup, Index of Multiple Deprivation and local-authority comparisons from the CES arts report.
observations.uncertainty: Deprivation is an area-level measure, not an individual income measure; local differences combine supply, transport, price, population composition, survey coverage and cultural preference.
observations.subgroup: People not engaging with arts, residents of the most and least deprived areas, and residents across English local authorities.
observations.counterinterpretation: A geographic participation gap does not identify whether price, venue supply, time, transport, welcome, safety, education or preference is the binding constraint.

observations.period: 2025/26; activity forms, age and socioeconomic sorting

denominator.unit: over 175,000 CES responses; people aged 16+ in England

cinema.unit: percent reporting cinema attendance as an arts event

reading.unit: percent reporting reading books, graphic novels or magazines as a physical arts activity

older_physical_engagement.value: people aged 45 to 84 were generally more likely than the England average to engage physically, while many adults aged 16 to 39 were less likely

socioeconomic_gradient.value: physical engagement ranged from 92% among higher managerial, administrative and professional occupations to 80% in routine and manual occupations and 66% among people who had never worked or were long-term unemployed

consumption_route.value: arts participation mixes cultural consumption and creation, with life stage and socioeconomic position shaping the available repertoire

observations.method: Descriptive demographic and activity-type estimates from the 2025/26 arts report.
observations.uncertainty: The estimates are self-reported and do not measure spending, repeat attendance, quality, social outcomes or the meaning of different activities to participants.
observations.subgroup: People aged 16+ by age, sex, disability, religion, ethnicity and socioeconomic classification.
observations.counterinterpretation: Different engagement rates may reflect activity definitions and life-stage routines rather than a simple hierarchy of cultural access or value.

related_sources.claim: Official release page with data-table, technical and update context.
CES programme guidance, coverage, pathways and survey design context.

boundary: This record adds an arts-participation route from household room, place and cultural repertoire through physical and digital engagement, local access, socioeconomic inequality and possible social connection. It is representative England survey evidence with a documented questionnaire and method discontinuity concern, not a causal explanation of participation decline, an attendance register, a spending measure, or a universal account of cultural value.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GOV.UK arts report reviewed for release update, survey frame, headline and time-series estimates, physical/digital split, barriers, demographic and deprivation gradients, local-authority variation, activity definitions and quality caveats.
